audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Job's answer to Zophar: demand for listening, wicked prosperity, peaceful death, rejection of simplistic retribution, and challenge to the friends' empty comfort.

verses.restored: Job answered and said:

familiar.text: But Job answered and said,

modern.text: Then Job answered:

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר

verses.restored: Listen carefully to my word, and let this be your comfort.

familiar.text: Hear diligently my speech, and let this be your consolations.

modern.text: “Listen carefully to my words; let this be your consolation to me.

original.text: שִׁמְע֣וּ שָׁ֭מוֹעַ מִלָּתִ֑י וּתְהִי זֹ֝֗את תַּנְח֥וּמֹֽתֵיכֶֽם

verses.restored: Bear with me, and I myself will speak; after I have spoken, you may mock.

familiar.text: Suffer me that I may speak; and after that I have spoken, mock on.

modern.text: Bear with me while I speak; then, after I have spoken, you may go on mocking.

original.text: שָׂ֭אוּנִי וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר וְאַחַ֖ר דַּבְּרִ֣י תַלְעִֽיג

verses.restored: As for me, is my complaint to a human? And why should my spirit not be impatient?

familiar.text: As for me, is my complaint to man? and if it were so, why should not my spirit be troubled?

modern.text: Is my complaint against a man? Then why should I not be impatient?

original.text: הֶ֭אָנֹכִי לְאָדָ֣ם שִׂיחִ֑י וְאִם מַ֝דּ֗וּעַ לֹא תִקְצַ֥ר רוּחִֽי

verses.restored: Turn to me and be appalled, and put a hand over your mouth.

familiar.text: Mark me, and be astonished, and lay your hand upon your mouth.

modern.text: Look at me and be appalled; put your hand over your mouth.

original.text: פְּנוּ אֵלַ֥י וְהָשַׁ֑מּוּ וְשִׂ֖ימוּ יָ֣ד עַל פֶּֽה

verses.restored: When I remember, I am terrified, and trembling seizes my flesh.

familiar.text: Even when I remember I am afraid, and trembling taketh hold on my flesh.

modern.text: When I remember, terror takes hold, and my body trembles in horror.

original.text: וְאִם זָכַ֥רְתִּי וְנִבְהָ֑לְתִּי וְאָחַ֥ז בְּ֝שָׂרִ֗י פַּלָּצֽוּת

verses.restored: Why do the wicked live, grow old, and even become mighty in power?

familiar.text: Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power?

modern.text: Why do the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power?

original.text: מַדּ֣וּעַ רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִחְי֑וּ עָ֝תְק֗וּ גַּם גָּ֥בְרוּ חָֽיִל

verses.restored: Their seed is established before them with them, and their offspring before their eyes.

familiar.text: Their seed is established in their sight with them, and their offspring before their eyes.

modern.text: Their descendants are established around them, and their offspring before their eyes.

original.text: זַרְעָ֤ם נָכ֣וֹן לִפְנֵיהֶ֣ם עִמָּ֑ם וְ֝צֶאֱצָאֵיהֶ֗ם לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Their houses are peace, without dread, and the rod of the Divine is not upon them.

familiar.text: Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them.

modern.text: Their homes are safe from fear; no rod of punishment from God is upon them.

original.text: בָּתֵּיהֶ֣ם שָׁל֣וֹם מִפָּ֑חַד וְלֹ֤א שֵׁ֖בֶט אֱל֣וֹהַּ עֲלֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Their bull breeds and does not fail; their cow calves and does not miscarry.

familiar.text: Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; their cow calveth, and casteth not her calf.

modern.text: Their bulls breed without fail; their cows bear calves and do not miscarry.

original.text: שׁוֹר֣וֹ עִ֭בַּר וְלֹ֣א יַגְעִ֑ל תְּפַלֵּ֥ט פָּ֝רָת֗וֹ וְלֹ֣א תְשַׁכֵּֽל

verses.restored: They send out their little ones like a flock, and their children dance.

familiar.text: They send forth their little ones like a flock, and their children dance.

modern.text: They send forth their little ones like a flock; their children skip about,

original.text: יְשַׁלְּח֣וּ כַ֭צֹּאן עֲוִילֵיהֶ֑ם וְ֝יַלְדֵיהֶ֗ם יְרַקֵּדֽוּן

verses.restored: They lift up tambourine and lyre and rejoice to the sound of the pipe.

familiar.text: They take the timbrel and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ.

modern.text: singing to the tambourine and lyre and making merry at the sound of the flute.

original.text: יִ֭שְׂאוּ כְּתֹ֣ף וְכִנּ֑וֹר וְ֝יִשְׂמְח֗וּ לְק֣וֹל עוּגָֽב

verses.restored: They spend their days in good, and in a moment they go down to Sheol.

familiar.text: They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave.

modern.text: They spend their days in prosperity and go down to Sheol in peace.

original.text: יבלו בַטּ֣וֹב יְמֵיהֶ֑ם וּ֝בְרֶ֗גַע שְׁא֣וֹל יֵחָֽתּוּ

verses.restored: Yet they say to the Divine, Depart from us; we do not desire knowledge of your ways.

familiar.text: Therefore they say unto God, Depart from us; for we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.

modern.text: Yet they say to God: ‘Leave us alone! For we have no desire to know Your ways.

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לָ֭אֵל ס֣וּר מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וְדַ֥עַת דְּ֝רָכֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א חָפָֽצְנוּ

verses.restored: What is Shaddai, that we should serve him? What profit do we have if we plead with him?

familiar.text: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what profit should we have, if we pray unto him?

modern.text: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve Him, and what would we gain if we pray to Him?’

original.text: מַה שַׁדַּ֥י כִּֽי נַֽעַבְדֶ֑נּוּ וּמַה נּ֝וֹעִ֗יל כִּ֣י נִפְגַּע בּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Look, their good is not in their hand. The counsel of the wicked is far from me.

familiar.text: Lo, their good is not in their hand: the counsel of the wicked is far from me.

modern.text: Still, their prosperity is not in their own hands, so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.

original.text: הֵ֤ן לֹ֣א בְיָדָ֣ם טוּבָ֑ם עֲצַ֥ת רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים רָ֣חֲקָה מֶֽנִּי

verses.restored: How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? Does their calamity come upon them? Does he apportion pains in his anger?

familiar.text: How oft is the candle of the wicked put out! and how oft cometh their destruction upon them! God distributeth sorrows in his anger.

modern.text: How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? Does disaster come upon them? Does God, in His anger, apportion destruction?

original.text: כַּמָּ֤ה נֵר רְשָׁ֘עִ֤ים יִדְעָ֗ךְ וְיָבֹ֣א עָלֵ֣ימוֹ אֵידָ֑ם חֲ֝בָלִ֗ים יְחַלֵּ֥ק בְּאַפּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Are they like straw before the wind, and like chaff that the storm steals away?

familiar.text: They are as stubble before the wind, and as chaff that the storm carrieth away.

modern.text: Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm?

original.text: יִהְי֗וּ כְּתֶ֥בֶן לִפְנֵי ר֑וּחַ וּ֝כְמֹ֗ץ גְּנָבַ֥תּוּ סוּפָֽה

verses.restored: You say, The Divine stores up his harm for his children. Let him repay the person himself, so that he may know it.

familiar.text: God layeth up his iniquity for his children: he rewardeth him, and he shall know it.

modern.text: It is said that God lays up one’s punishment for his children. Let God repay the man himself, so he will know it.

original.text: אֱל֗וֹהַּ יִצְפֹּן לְבָנָ֥יו אוֹנ֑וֹ יְשַׁלֵּ֖ם אֵלָ֣יו וְיֵדָֽע

verses.restored: Let his own eyes see his ruin, and let him drink from the wrath of Shaddai.

familiar.text: His eyes shall see his destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty.

modern.text: Let his eyes see his own destruction; let him drink for himself the wrath of the Almighty.

original.text: יִרְא֣וּ עינו כִּיד֑וֹ וּמֵחֲמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י יִשְׁתֶּֽה

verses.restored: For what is his delight in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off?

familiar.text: For what pleasure hath he in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off in the midst?

modern.text: For what does he care about his household after him, when the number of his months has run out?

original.text: כִּ֤י מַה חֶפְצ֣וֹ בְּבֵית֣וֹ אַחֲרָ֑יו וּמִסְפַּ֖ר חֳדָשָׁ֣יו חֻצָּֽצוּ

verses.restored: Will anyone teach knowledge to the Divine, since he judges those on high?

familiar.text: Shall any teach God knowledge? seeing he judgeth those that are high.

modern.text: Can anyone teach knowledge to God, since He judges those on high?

original.text: הַלְאֵ֥ל יְלַמֶּד דָּ֑עַת וְ֝ה֗וּא רָמִ֥ים יִשְׁפּֽוֹט

verses.restored: One dies in his full strength, wholly at ease and secure,

familiar.text: One dieth in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.

modern.text: One man dies full of vigor, completely secure and at ease.

original.text: זֶ֗ה יָ֭מוּת בְּעֶ֣צֶם תֻּמּ֑וֹ כֻּ֝לּ֗וֹ שַׁלְאֲנַ֥ן וְשָׁלֵֽיו

verses.restored: his pails full of milk, and the marrow of his bones moist.

familiar.text: His breasts are full of milk, and his bones are moistened with marrow.

modern.text: His body is well nourished, and his bones are rich with marrow.

original.text: עֲ֭טִינָיו מָלְא֣וּ חָלָ֑ב וּמֹ֖חַ עַצְמוֹתָ֣יו יְשֻׁקֶּֽה

verses.restored: Another dies with bitter soul, never having eaten good.

familiar.text: And another dieth in the bitterness of his soul, and never eateth with pleasure.

modern.text: Yet another man dies in the bitterness of his soul, having never tasted prosperity.

original.text: וְזֶ֗ה יָ֭מוּת בְּנֶ֣פֶשׁ מָרָ֑ה וְלֹֽא אָ֝כַ֗ל בַּטּוֹבָֽה

verses.restored: Together they lie down in the dust, and worms cover them.

familiar.text: They shall lie down alike in the dust, and the worms shall cover them.

modern.text: But together they lie down in the dust, and worms cover them both.

original.text: יַ֭חַד עַל עָפָ֣ר יִשְׁכָּ֑בוּ וְ֝רִמָּ֗ה תְּכַסֶּ֥ה עֲלֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Look, I know your thoughts and the schemes by which you would wrong me.

familiar.text: Behold, I know your thoughts, and the devices which ye wrongfully imagine against me.

modern.text: Behold, I know your thoughts full well, the schemes by which you would wrong me.

original.text: הֵ֣ן יָ֭דַעְתִּי מַחְשְׁבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וּ֝מְזִמּ֗וֹת עָלַ֥י תַּחְמֹֽסוּ

verses.restored: For you say, Where is the house of the noble one? Where is the tent, the dwelling of the wicked?

familiar.text: For ye say, Where is the house of the prince? and where are the dwelling places of the wicked?

modern.text: For you say, ‘Where now is the nobleman’s house, and where are the tents in which the wicked dwell?’

original.text: כִּ֤י תֹֽאמְר֗וּ אַיֵּ֥ה בֵית נָדִ֑יב וְ֝אַיֵּ֗ה אֹ֤הֶל מִשְׁכְּנ֬וֹת רְשָׁעִֽים

verses.restored: Have you not asked those who travel the roads, and do you not recognize their signs?

familiar.text: Have ye not asked them that go by the way? and do ye not know their tokens,

modern.text: Have you never asked those who travel the roads? Do you not accept their reports?

original.text: הֲלֹ֣א שְׁ֭אֶלְתֶּם ע֣וֹבְרֵי דָ֑רֶךְ וְ֝אֹתֹתָ֗ם לֹ֣א תְנַכֵּֽרוּ

verses.restored: That the evil person is spared in the day of calamity; they are led away in the day of wrath.

familiar.text: That the wicked is reserved to the day of destruction? they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath.

modern.text: Indeed, the evil man is spared from the day of calamity, delivered from the day of wrath.

original.text: כִּ֤י לְי֣וֹם אֵ֭יד יֵחָ֣שֶׂךְ רָ֑ע לְי֖וֹם עֲבָר֣וֹת יוּבָֽלוּ

verses.restored: Who declares his way to his face? And who repays him for what he has done?

familiar.text: Who shall declare his way to his face? and who shall repay him what he hath done?

modern.text: Who denounces his behavior to his face? Who repays him for what he has done?

original.text: מִֽי יַגִּ֣יד עַל פָּנָ֣יו דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וְהֽוּא עָ֝שָׂ֗ה מִ֣י יְשַׁלֶּם לֽוֹ

verses.restored: He is carried to the burial place, and watch is kept over his tomb.

familiar.text: Yet shall he be brought to the grave, and shall remain in the tomb.

modern.text: He is carried to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb.

original.text: וְ֭הוּא לִקְבָר֣וֹת יוּבָ֑ל וְֽעַל גָּדִ֥ישׁ יִשְׁקֽוֹד

verses.restored: The clods of the valley are sweet to him; all humanity follows after him, and those before him are without number.

familiar.text: The clods of the valley shall be sweet unto him, and every man shall draw after him, as there are innumerable before him.

modern.text: The clods of the valley are sweet to him; everyone follows behind him, and those before him are without number.

original.text: מָֽתְקוּ ל֗וֹ רִגְבֵ֫י נָ֥חַל וְ֭אַחֲרָיו כָּל אָדָ֣ם יִמְשׁ֑וֹךְ וּ֝לְפָנָ֗יו אֵ֣ין מִסְפָּֽר

verses.restored: So how will you comfort me with emptiness? Nothing is left of your answers but betrayal.

familiar.text: How then comfort ye me in vain, seeing in your answers there remaineth falsehood?

modern.text: So how can you comfort me with empty words? For your answers remain full of falsehood.”

original.text: וְ֭אֵיךְ תְּנַחֲמ֣וּנִי הָ֑בֶל וּ֝תְשֽׁוּבֹתֵיכֶ֗ם נִשְׁאַר מָֽעַל
